
Discontinuities of the decay chain: resets of a state at a time or at a root, switches of the
right-hand side, a terminating root, and input data. The sensitivities take every jump, also where
a parameter moves the time of the jump. Mechanism and transport of the sensitivities:
[Events, switches and saltation](methods-events.html).

```{r library}
library(cppDE)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Model definition

`events` of [`cppODE()`](../reference/cppODE.html) is a data frame with one row per event:

| column | content |
|:--|:--|
| `var` | the state that is reset |
| `time` | the event time, a number or an expression of the parameters |
| `root` | a root expression of states, parameters and `time`; the event fires where it crosses zero |
| `value` | the value, a number or an expression of states, parameters and `time` |
| `method` | `"replace"` (default), `"add"` or `"multiply"` |

Each row has exactly one of `time` and `root`, the other `NA`. Below, a dose of $A$ at `t_e`, a
loss of $B$ by the factor `f` at `t_e + delay`, and a refill of $A$ by `dose` whenever $A$ falls
to `Amin`.

```{r events-model}
eqns  <- c(A = "-k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B")
parms <- c(A = 1, B = 0, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2)
times <- seq(0, 10, by = 0.1)

events <- data.frame(var    = c("A", "B", "A"),
                     time   = c("t_e", "t_e + delay", NA),
                     root   = c(NA, NA, "A - Amin"),
                     value  = c("dose", "f", "dose"),
                     method = c("add", "multiply", "add"))
dosed <- cppODE(eqns, events = events, modelname = "g2_dosed", compile = FALSE)
halved <- cppODE(eqns, events = data.frame(var = "B", time = "t_e", value = "B/2"),
                 modelname = "g2_halved", compile = FALSE)
```

`rootfunc`, a vector of expressions, ends the solve at the first zero crossing of any of them.
A switch is a comparison on a state or on `time` in the right-hand side, also inside
`piecewise()`, `ifelse()`, `Heaviside()` or `sign()`. `forcings` names input data.

```{r other-models}
stopped <- cppODE(eqns, rootfunc = "B - Bmax", modelname = "g2_stopped", compile = FALSE)
pulse   <- cppODE(c(A = "piecewise(u, time >= t1 && time < t2, 0) - k1*A",
                    B = "k1*A - k2*B"), modelname = "g2_pulse", compile = FALSE)
slide   <- cppODE(c(x = "-k*x + p*(x < xc)"), modelname = "g2_slide", compile = FALSE)
forced  <- cppODE(c(A = "u - k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B"), forcings = "u",
                  modelname = "g2_forced", compile = FALSE)

compile(dosed, halved, stopped, pulse, slide, forced, output = "guide2", cores = 2)
attr(dosed, "parameters")
```

## Events

The symbols of the event columns are parameters of the model. `maxroot` of
[`solveODE()`](../reference/solveODE.html) caps the firings per root event (default 1), `roottol`
is the tolerance of the root location.

```{r events, fig.height = 4.2}
pE   <- c(parms, t_e = 2, dose = 1, delay = 3, f = 0.5, Amin = 0.3)
outE <- solveODE(dosed, times, pE, maxroot = 3)

ggplot(longFormat(outE, sens = FALSE), aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3)
```

A time event inside the output window adds the event time to the output, with the state after the
event. A root event adds two rows, the states before and after the reset.

```{r event-rows}
nrow(outE$variable)
before <- which(diff(outE$time) < 1e-12)
cbind(time = outE$time, outE$variable)[sort(c(before, before + 1)), ]
```

The sensitivities in the event parameters include the shift of the event times:

```{r event-sens}
outE$tangent[nrow(outE$variable), , c("t_e", "delay", "dose", "f", "Amin")]
```

A `value` may read the states: `"B/2"` with `"replace"` halves $B$.

```{r replace}
outH <- solveODE(halved, times, c(parms, t_e = 2))
outH$variable[outH$time == 2, ]
```

A time event at the first output time applies before the solve starts; one before the first or at
or after the last output time is ignored.

## Terminating root

The solve ends at the first zero of a `rootfunc` expression, here when $B$ reaches `Bmax`.

```{r rootfunc}
outR <- solveODE(stopped, times, c(parms, Bmax = 0.4))
tail(cbind(time = outR$time, outR$variable), 2)
```

`rootfunc = "equilibrate"` ends at a steady state instead ([chapter 5](guide-steady-states.html)).

## Switches

The solver locates every switch of the right-hand side as a root and continues on the other
branch, so a short pulse is not stepped over. A switch adds no output row and does not count
towards `maxroot`. The sensitivities in `t1` and `t2` come from the jump of the right-hand side.

```{r pulse, fig.height = 4.2}
outP <- solveODE(pulse, times, c(A = 0, B = 0, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2, u = 1, t1 = 1, t2 = 1.5))

ggplot(longFormat(outP, "B"), aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3)
```

Where both branches point onto the switching surface, the solution slides along it
([sliding](methods-events.html#sliding)). Above `xc` the state decays, below it grows towards
`p/k`; it reaches `xc` and stays, and depends on `xc` alone from then on. $\partial x/\partial p$
is zero throughout and left out.

```{r slide, fig.height = 3}
outS <- solveODE(slide, times, c(x = 2, k = 1, p = 3, xc = 1))

ggplot(subset(longFormat(outS), panel != "∂x/∂p"), aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3)
```

`floor()`, `round()`, `abs()`, `max()` and the other kinks and steps take parameters and forcings
only: on a state or on the time they are an error, since no root locates them. Write such a step
with comparisons, see [expressions](../reference/expressions.html).

## Forcings

A forcing is input data, given to `solveODE()` as a named list of data frames with columns `time`
and `value`. The model sees the monotone cubic Hermite interpolant of the points, constant outside
them; [`forcingValues()`](../reference/forcingValues.html) evaluates it the same way.

```{r forcings, fig.height = 3}
tu   <- seq(0, 10, by = 0.5)
u    <- list(u = data.frame(time = tu, value = 1 + sin(tu)))
outF <- solveODE(forced, times, parms, forcings = u)
dimnames(outF$tangent)$sens

input <- data.frame(time = times, panel = "u", value = forcingValues(times, u)[, "u"])
ggplot(rbind(input, longFormat(outF, sens = FALSE)), aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = transform(u$u, panel = "u"), size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3)
```

A forcing is data, not a parameter, and has no sensitivity.
